Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: Psalm 16:1 verse illustration for Scripture for Life.
Input image: style reference only, Psalm 23:2 approved watercolor; make a new scene, not an edit.
Primary request: A small lone traveler in a simple undyed ancient robe rests safely within the natural shelter of a great limestone outcrop, looking out over a quiet Judean valley after rain. Refuge and preservation conveyed by the sheltering rock, no enemy or battle. Symbolic response to 'Preserve me, O God, for in You I take refuge'; not a reconstruction of an event.
Style/medium: Match the reference's finely detailed naturalistic watercolor, luminous washes, delicate grasses, warm ivory light, muted sage and forest greens, warm stone, subtle paper grain. Peaceful and reverent.
Composition: wide landscape 3:2, sheltered traveler small in the foreground, atmospheric hills beyond; fully painted to edges.
Constraints: one standalone painting, no panels, no text, no lettering, no border, no watermark, no modern objects, no depiction of God or divine human body.

Psalm 16:2, the goodness received from God. A close low view of a simple clay bowl of fresh figs and a small rustic loaf on a flat limestone beside an ancient olive tree, with dew on grass and an abundant sunlit valley beyond. Humble gratitude rather than riches; no people. Warm morning light, intimate still life in a spacious landscape.

Psalm 16:3, delight in the faithful community. A small gathering of five ordinary adults in modest ancient linen garments, seen at a respectful distance, sit in companionship beneath an olive grove overlooking terraces. Gentle delight, simple community, no feast spectacle.

Psalm 16:4, refusing divided worship. A lone traveler in plain ancient robes deliberately walks away from an unlit stone ritual platform and untouched dark clay pouring vessel toward an open olive-lined footpath. No blood, no violence, no readable markings, no idol body, no named character. The abandoned vessel small and shadowed in the foreground; the traveler and open country carry the scene. Sober restraint, clear choice.
